meta.title: Lawsuits, nuclear verdicts and civil justice, 17 days of posts
meta.subject: civil justice and tort reform in Texas — Texans for Lawsuit Reform and its opponents, nuclear verdicts and damages caps, trucking and commercial litigation rules, the business courts and the Fifteenth Court of Appeals, insurance rates and litigation costs, and claims of lawsuit abuse
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 17, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Texas lawsuits, nuclear verdicts and civil justice, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Lawsuit abuse as hidden tax
lanes.description: Frivolous suits and billboard-lawyer litigation add thousands of dollars in hidden costs to every Texas family, so lawmakers should rein in lawsuit abuse.

lanes.label: Nuclear verdicts drive up premiums
lanes.description: Outsized jury awards against trucking and commercial defendants inflate insurance rates and consumer prices, justifying damages caps and tighter litigation rules.

lanes.label: TLR as a political power broker
lanes.description: Texans for Lawsuit Reform is a donor-funded machine that buys influence in Texas politics, and is attacked as insincere, insider-driven, or hostile to particular candidates, sometimes from within the right.

lanes.label: Tort reform shields corporations
lanes.description: Caps and litigation limits let corporations and insurers escape accountability and leave injured Texans, workers, and families without remedy while trial lawyers defend access to the courts.

lanes.label: Business courts and Fifteenth Court
lanes.description: The Texas business courts and Fifteenth Court of Appeals are argued over as either efficient, expert forums or tilted venues that favor corporations and the state's political leadership.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.
